info.title: Data Hub API
info.description: Integrator REST API for Data Hub. Authenticate with a personal access token (`Authorization: Bearer dhub_…`). Session cookies also work for browser callers.

servers.description: Relative to your Data Hub host

bearerAuth.description: Personal access tokens begin with `dhub_…` and are restricted by their assigned scopes.

past_watcher_count.description: How many deregistered watchers the instrument has had.

hostname.description: The PC the watcher runs on. Needs scope `watchers:read`; left out without it.

os_info.description: The PC's operating system. Needs scope `watchers:read`; left out without it.

version.description: Installed watcher version. Null until its first heartbeat. Needs scope `watchers:read`; left out without it.

status.description: Detailed watcher status. `stale` means no heartbeat for 5 minutes, or no return from a restart within 15.

status_reason.description: Why the watcher is waiting (the missing folder), or why it stopped for a restart (`system_shutdown` or `auto_update`). The reason stays while the status reads `stale`.

watch_directory.description: The folder the watcher watches. Needs scope `watchers:read`; left out without it.

file_patterns.description: File patterns from the watcher's config, in config order.

config_state.description: State of the watcher's settings: `pending` (a change is waiting for the watcher), `rejected` (the watcher refused the latest change), `edited_on_pc` (a PC edit takes effect when the watcher restarts), `applied`, or `none`.

shared_computer_with.description: Other instruments whose active watchers run on the same computer (hostnames compared without case). Needs scope `watchers:read`; left out without it.

InstrumentWatcher.description: An instrument's one active watcher: the program on the instrument PC that finds new files and uploads them. `hostname`, `os_info`, `version`, `watch_directory` and `shared_computer_with` say where it runs, so they need scope `watchers:read` as well as `instruments:read`. A token without it gets a watcher with those five fields absent. Browser sessions hold every scope.

state.description: `online`: the watcher checked in within 5 minutes. `restarting`: the watcher stopped for a Windows restart or an automatic update less than 15 minutes ago. `connecting`: the watcher registered and hasn't sent a heartbeat yet, for up to 15 minutes after it registered or the instrument was confirmed; after that the instrument is `offline` with reason `never_checked_in`. `offline`: anything else. The instrument's own status plays no part: a pending instrument can be `online`.

reason.description: Why the instrument is offline. Null in every other state.

InstrumentConnection.description: Whether new files can reach Data Hub, and why not.

watcher_count.description: Deprecated. An instrument has at most one watcher: use `watcher`, which is null when it has none.

files_upload_failed.description: Files the watcher gave up on (`upload_failed`).

files_waiting_upload.description: Files on their way from the instrument PC: requested, or ones the watcher uploads on its own.

files_not_uploaded.description: Files only on the instrument PC that nothing will upload until someone requests them.

status.description: The status Data Hub shows for the watcher. `stale` is worked out when you ask and is never stored. A `watching` or `waiting` watcher is `stale` when its last heartbeat is more than 5 minutes old. A `stopped` watcher stays `stopped`, however old its last heartbeat, unless it stopped for a restart or an update (see `status_reason`): then it is `stale` when its last heartbeat is more than 15 minutes old. A `registered` watcher, which hasn't sent its first heartbeat, is `stale` 15 minutes after it registered, or after its instrument was confirmed if that came later; while its instrument is pending it stays `registered`. A deregistered watcher is always `stopped`. The `status` filter on the list endpoint returns the watchers that show that status.

status_reason.description: Why the watcher is `waiting` (for example a missing watch folder), or why it stopped for a restart: `system_shutdown` for Windows shutting down or restarting, `auto_update` for an automatic update (watcher 1.4.2 and later send it). It is the reason of the watcher's last heartbeat, so it stays while `status` reads `stale`. It is null when that heartbeat was any other status, or a stop that gave no such reason.

post.description: Requires scope `runs:create`. PAT only; browser sessions are rejected. Returns 200 with the existing run when it already exists. Returns 409 (`details.reason: run_deleted`) when the run exists and was deleted and the body has `source: "watcher"`, an `acquired_at`, or a non-empty `detected_files`. The request then attaches no files and changes nothing. A body with only `run_id` and `source: "lambda"` still gets 200. A token that registered a watcher may act only on instruments whose active watcher it registered, and gets 403 for any other.

post.description: Requires scope `runs:reprocess`. Queues every `uploaded`, `failed`, `completed`, or stalled `processing` raw file on the run for reprocessing. Each file starts as soon as a processing slot is free (at most 10 raw files process at once by default), and a file that does not start right away waits as `queued`. `files_queued` counts every file accepted, whether it started or is waiting. Processed artifacts are skipped. The instrument must have a Lambda processor. A token that registered a watcher may act only on instruments whose active watcher it registered, and gets 403 for any other.

Works on a soft-deleted run too. `files_cancelled` is 0 when no file was queued. post.description: Requires scope `runs:upload`. PAT only; browser sessions are rejected. Watchers at 1.1.0 or newer send `relative_path` and `X-Data-Hub-Watcher-Version`. A file whose name is already used by a different folder is stored as `<stem>~<folder hash>.<ext>`, and the returned `s3_key` uses that stored name. Older watchers are looked up by filename only. Watchers at 1.2.0 or newer receive a multipart upload for files of 100 MB or more. Older watchers are refused when the file is over 5 GB. Returns 409 (`details.reason: run_deleted`) when the run was deleted. A token that registered a watcher may act only on instruments whose active watcher it registered, and gets 403 for any other.

post.description: Requires scope `lab-notebooks:write`. A lab notebook is one page, such as a Notion page. Send `runs` to add runs in the same request; each one gets its own outcome, as in `POST /lab-notebooks/{labNotebookId}/runs`. Returns 409 when another lab notebook already has the page, deleted ones included: `details.lab_notebook_id` names that lab notebook and `details.deleted` says whether it is deleted. Restore a deleted one instead. Returns 400 when `owner_id` names no user. A token that registered a watcher gets 403. It may only add its own instrument's runs to a lab notebook and remove them.

owner_id.description: The user who owns the lab notebook. Left out or null, it has no owner. `"me"` means the signed-in person, so a token can't use it.

runs.description: Runs to add as the lab notebook is created, at most 100. They can belong to different instruments.

status_reason.description: Why the watcher is `waiting`, for example a missing watch folder. On a `stopped` heartbeat, `system_shutdown` says the watcher stopped because Windows is shutting down or restarting (watcher 1.4.1 and later send it), and `auto_update` says it stopped to install an automatic update and start again (watcher 1.4.2 and later send it). Data Hub keeps these two reasons on the watcher, keeps the instrument's requested uploads queued for the watcher to upload after it starts again, and cancels them only if no heartbeat arrives for about 15 minutes. After that long without a heartbeat the watcher shows as `stale`. Any other `stopped` heartbeat cancels the requested uploads at once, and its reason is not kept.
